title: Lesson Plan — Algebraic Expressions and Polynomials (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Identify variables, constants, terms, coefficients and the constant term in a given algebraic expression.
Distinguish like terms from unlike terms and combine like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients.
Classify a given expression as a monomial, binomial, trinomial or multinomial after simplification.
Decide whether an expression is a polynomial and, if so, find its degree and write it in standard form.
Add, subtract and multiply polynomials using either the horizontal or vertical method, and use the laws of exponents during multiplication.
Evaluate a polynomial at a given value of the variable and verify whether a given number is a zero of the polynomial.
prerequisites: Class 9 ideas of algebraic expressions, like / unlike terms and basic substitution.
Comfort with the integer arithmetic of signed numbers (positive × positive, negative × negative etc.).
Laws of exponents from Chapter 2 (especially x^a · x^b = x^(a+b)).
Familiarity with the distributive law a(b + c) = ab + ac.
materials: Index cards labelled with assorted expressions (3/x, x^2 + 1, √x, 7, x^(−2) + 1, 4xy + 5x^2 y^3) for the polynomial-vs-not sort
Pre-printed reference sheet with the five laws of exponents (one per pair, recycled from Chapter 2)
Worksheet handout (Worksheet — Algebraic Expressions and Polynomials)
A4 sheet with the FOIL acronym diagram (First, Outer, Inner, Last) for visual reinforcement

activities.description: Hook the class with a tiny puzzle. Write 3x + 5 on the board and ask 'How many terms? What's the coefficient of x? What does this expression evaluate to when x = 4?' Then write 3/x and ask 'Is THIS the same kind of object?' Collect guesses without confirming. Promise the answer in the Explain phase.
teacher_actions: Elicit answers about terms, coefficients and substitution for 3x + 5.
Pause on 3/x and let students disagree before revealing it is NOT a polynomial.
student_actions: Call out coefficients and term counts.
Make a prediction about whether 3/x is a polynomial; record their guess.
Note the question 'why isn't 3/x a polynomial?' for the Explain phase.

activities.description: Pair card sort. Distribute index cards (3/x, x^2 + 1, √x, 7, x^(−2) + 1, 4xy + 5x^2 y^3, 3x − 5, 2x^3) and ask pairs to sort them into 'polynomial' and 'not a polynomial'. Use the disagreements as diagnostic data — 7 (constant) and 4xy + 5x^2 y^3 (multi-variable) are the typical surprises.
teacher_actions: Distribute the card stacks; circulate to listen for the diagnostic disagreements.
Pick two pairs to share their classifications before launching the Explain phase.
Hold a tally of which cards generated the most disagreement.
student_actions: Sort cards collaboratively; verbalise each placement.
Tag one card they were unsure about for whole-class discussion.

activities.description: Direct instruction in four blocks: (i) vocabulary (variable, constant, term, coefficient, like terms) with a short worked example; (ii) classification by number of terms (monomial → multinomial); (iii) polynomial definition + degree + standard form, using the card-sort cards as anchors; (iv) addition / subtraction (horizontal and vertical) followed by multiplication (monomial × poly, FOIL, vertical long-multiplication). Drive home one big idea: 'a polynomial uses only whole-number powers and never divides by a variable'.
teacher_actions: Build the vocabulary table on the board with one example per row.
Resolve the card-sort disagreements with the polynomial definition.
Long-derive (x + 2)(x + 3) live on the board with FOIL labelled on each step.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate each worked example in their notebooks.
Predict the next step before the teacher writes it.
Add the FOIL diagram to a 'rules box' for quick reference.

activities.description: Guided practice. Students work through six worksheet problems: two on identifying coefficients and terms, one on classifying degree of a multi-variable polynomial, one on adding two polynomials vertically, one on (x + 5)(x − 2) using FOIL, and one on evaluating p(x) = x^2 − 4x + 4 at x = 2 and x = 3 (showing x = 2 is a zero).
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a stuck student.
Collect common slips (e.g. forgetting the sign in front of a term) for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve the problems individually first, then compare with a bench partner.
Self-check against the posted answer key after the first three problems.
Ask a peer before asking the teacher.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: an 8-question MCQ + short-answer slip with at least one item per content area drawn from the chapter's question bank. Students complete it silently in 9 minutes; the teacher then projects answers and runs a 4-minute discussion focused on the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute the exit ticket; remind students it is individual work.
Time the quiz to 9 minutes strictly.
Tally results quickly and address the top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection on any item they got wrong.

activities.description: Set homework: complete the rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Write a quadratic polynomial in standard form whose leading coefficient is 2, whose constant term is −5 and which has x = 1 as a zero. Verify by substitution.' Preview the next chapter (Special Products and Factorisation) by writing (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 on the board and noting that we just used FOIL to derive exactly this kind of identity.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and the CREATE prompt.
Bridge to the next chapter with the (a + b)^2 expansion.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet and the FOIL reference sheet for home study.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Algebraic Expressions and Polynomials handout.
Write a quadratic polynomial in standard form with leading coefficient 2, constant term −5 and x = 1 as a zero; verify by substitution.
From the chapter-summary glossary, pick three terms and write one original example sentence using each correctly.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket described in the Evaluate phase as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question MCQ quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.

Mark the LONG_ANSWER question on multiplying (x^2 − 2x + 3)(x + 4) using the auto-grade rubric — verify that all four products are taken, like terms combined, and result is 2x^3-equivalent in standard form.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (standard form correct? root verified by substitution?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 3: Algebraic Expressions and Polynomials.
NCERT Class 9 Mathematics, Chapter 2: Polynomials (for the prerequisite vocabulary).
